calls.reason: The 2029 deadline has not passed. Tesla and Lyft describe planned customer-car services for 2027, but the packet documents no qualifying paid driverless operation.
Waymo's 2023 paper disclosed remote guidance without quantifying its contribution. The packet lacks an industry-wide comparison, leaving Marcus's hedged generalization unsettled.
CNBC authenticated Cruise's report of remote assistance for 2–4% of operating time and requests every four to five miles. That supports the central claim of recurring calls for remote help.

CRS reported no Level 5 deployment in July 2025, but the packet does not establish heavy call-center dependence across all programs. The forecast also leaves its timing undefined and hedges the deception claim.

The Register reported 1.5 support workers per vehicle and Cruise's acknowledgment of overstaffing. GM disclosed a $732 million quarterly adjusted loss, supporting the ordinary reading of an overstaffed, loss-making operation.

The Swiss Re comparison excluded onboard drivers but did not exclude remote guidance; Waymo's simulation study offers a possible exception. These examples do not settle the broader claim about nearly all comparisons.
